meta.method: Products read from each retailer's own US product pages or the JSON those pages load (Shopify product JSON for Everlane/Allbirds/Timex; Gap Inc. search API + product pages for Gap/Old Navy/Banana Republic; Zara US ?ajax=true product data + composition panel; Uniqlo US commerce API details; nike.com __NEXT_DATA__; J.Crew and Brooks Brothers JSON-LD + page text; Pandora/Fossil/Prada page text; Clarks/Dr. Martens/Seiko/Nordstrom pages via fetch). Retailers whose sites block automated reads (Levi's, H&M, adidas, lululemon, Ray-Ban, Casio, Coach, Macy's, Ralph Lauren) come from search-result snippets and are marked confirmed:false. Target pages render price client-side, so Target items have page-confirmed name/colors/sizes/fabric but snippet or missing prices (confirmed:false).
meta.priceConvention: price = regular (list/compare-at) price in USD before sales tax; salePrice/priceNote record markdowns seen on 2026-10-01. Sales tax is not included.
meta.careConvention: care is one of "machine wash" | "hand wash" | "dry clean only" for garments, classified from the page text kept in careText; null for footwear, bags, belts, sunglasses, jewelry and watches, or where the page gave no instruction.
meta.sizesConvention: sizes are the option labels the product page offers, in the retailer's own notation (Gap/Old Navy W/L, Uniqlo "inch", Brooks Brothers decoded from codes, e.g. 40R, 32x32, 10.5 D). An empty array means the size list could not be read.
gaps: Gucci: search provider refuses gucci.com, so Prada and Ralph Lauren Purple Label are the luxury houses.
Nordstrom: two more Nordstrom-brand items were read but are sold out with no price, so they were left out.
Target: prices for 3 of 5 items were not captured (client-side rendering).

Store presence lists only cities where a store was found in a 2026 source; New Haven has very few of these chains inside city limits (J.Crew and lululemon at The Shops at Yale; Target and Old Navy are in neighbouring North Haven/Hamden).
